- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",

"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.

Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. caller-supplied backing store; MmapBacking maps a file (one page above

=== 798e897 ===
798e897 feat(hybrid): minimal drain (mcycle/minstret only) for unverified runs
When --verify is off the driver consumes only the vsim mcycle delta, so the
full register-file readback at the exit drain -- ~190 DMI abstract commands
(f0..f31, the V dump sweep, the Andes/M-ext CSR blocks) -- is wasted wall-clock
that never affects the cycle figure. Add StateDrain::drain_counters_only(),
which halts, reads just mcycle+minstret, and passes every other field through
from the QEMU1 snapshot. HandoffController::set_minimal_drain() routes the exit
drain to it; the new --drain-minimal flag threads through enable_hybrid_handoff.
Default off, so --verify and existing callers keep the full drain.

For a scalar hello this cuts the drain phase from ~11.7s to ~0.15s (total
hybrid run ~27s -> ~12s) with the cycle figure unchanged.

=== 1663d67 ===
1663d67 perf(hybrid): batch the V-data sweep into fewer Program-Buffer executions
The V-register sweep issued one Program-Buffer execution per register plus one
abstract x7 write per register -- 33 PB executions + 32 x7 writes each
direction. Each is a halted-hart Debug-Module round-trip (~1000 sim cycles
spent in the busy-poll), so the cost is the NUMBER of executions, not the bytes
moved (the data itself rides the shared mmap).

Pack (vle8.v/vse8.v ; addi) pairs into each execution and advance the base
pointer x7 with the in-buffer addi, so x7 is staged ONCE and 32 registers cost
ceil(32/7)=5 executions: 33 -> 6 PB executions and 32 -> 1 x7 write per
direction (~67 -> ~9 DM round-trips). x7 persists across executions (the hart
stays halted), so each batch resumes advancing where the last stopped. Adds
encode_addi.

The drained V state is byte-identical: verified by --verify (state-diff) on
rt_c_v_regs, rt_c_v_csrs, and rt_c_v_matmul against the QEMU oracle.

Building on the batched sweep, transport all 32 V registers with RVV LMUL=8:
one vsetvl to e8/m8 (vl=8*vlenb) then 4 grouped vle8.v/vse8.v (v0/v8/v16/v24)

drops from 6 PB executions + per-register x7 writes to 2 executions (vsetvl +
one grouped) and one x7 write -- roughly 9 -> 5 DM round-trips per direction.

Requires the scratch packed at vlenb stride (stage_v_to_scratch) so 8
consecutive registers are contiguous for a grouped unit-stride access; the
sweep drops its stride argument and derives the group span from vlenb. The
wire-slot padding stays zero, so --verify still compares byte-identical.

fields, all 32 V registers byte-identical to the QEMU oracle); window_cycles

=== 05f2750 ===
05f2750 fix(mem): make the final word of a memory region reachable (behavioral)
SimpleMemory's bounds check called region.contains({addr, addr + len}).
That braced temporary runs through MemoryRegion's ctor, which treats its
second argument as an INCLUSIVE end and stores end_address = arg + 1. But
addr + len is already the EXCLUSIVE end of the access, so the temporary
spanned [addr, addr + len + 1) -- one byte too long. contains() then
required addr + len + 1 <= region.end_address, rejecting any access whose
exclusive end landed exactly on end_address: the final word of a region was
unreachable (TLM_ADDRESS_ERROR).

Never hit before because nothing parked data at the exact top of a region;
the hybrid V-scratch GPR page puts x31 in that final word, so the resume
ld-sweep silently dropped it.

Add MemoryRegion::contains_access(addr, len) -- a half-open range check that
does NOT round the end up -- and use it in SimpleMemory. It is strictly more
permissive than the old check: it admits exactly the previously-rejected
final-byte accesses and rejects nothing that already worked, so no fixture
can regress. RED: simple_memory "final word of the region" case + a
memory_region contains_access case; both green after the fix.

content.content:
747e209 refactor(hybrid): remove legacy PB CSR-sweep restore path
ResumeDriver's Andes+M-ext CSR restore had two paths: the default
per-CSR Abstract Command, and an opt-in Program-Buffer batch sweep
(set_csr_sweep/HYBRID_RESTORE_CSR_SWEEP). The batch sweep couldn't
tolerate a cmderr on one CSR without corrupting the rest of the batch,
unlike the abstract path's per-CSR clear_cmderr -- so it stayed off by
default and is now removed entirely. CSR restore is Abstract Command +
LG1 liveness gating only; GPR/FPR/V registers keep their existing PB
block-load paths, and the drain-side CSR sweep is unaffected (csrr
reads can't fault the way csrrw writes can).

80ab50d refactor(hybrid): remove GPR/FPR/CSR Program-Buffer sweeps -- transport is Abstract-Command-only
Behavioral. Register/CSR transport now uses one Abstract Command per
GPR/FPR/CSR in BOTH directions; the Program Buffer carries only state the
abstract command space cannot reach (V data sweep, Tier-B vsetvl, L2C MMIO).

Removed wholesale, no opt-outs left behind:
- ResumeDriver: set_gpr/fpr_block_load, restore_gprs/fprs_via_pb
- StateDrain: set_gpr/fpr_block_store, set_csr_sweep + the csrr+sd sweep
- HandoffController: set_block_store_drain / set_csr_sweep forwarders
- Simulator: GPR/FPR scratch staging, HYBRID_RESTORE_{GPR,FPR}_BLOCK env
  toggles, CSR scratch lift (lift_scratch_blocks is V-only now),
  hybrid_drain_minimal_
- v_regfile_xfer: GPR/FPR/CSR scratch layout + stage/lift helpers;
  for_each_sweep_csr renamed for_each_transport_csr (slot index dropped)
- program_buffer: pb_block_sweep, csr_sweep, CsrSweepDir, encode_{ld,sd,
  fld,fsd,csrrs}

The scratch page now carries only the V regfile. Rationale: the abstract
path's per-CSR cmderr-clear tolerates a single WARL/read-only fault where a
batched PB program cannot; drain cost moved off the measured window (mcycle
is read before the CSR drain), and --verify off already uses the minimal
counters-only drain. Caps over-claims now surface as --verify field diffs
instead of the sweep's bisect throw.

Tests: contract tests pin abstract-only in both directions (no PB execution
on non-V, non-L2C state); walker gating/order coverage moved to
for_each_transport_csr. 17/17 hybrid unit tests, e2e 43 passed / 0 failed /
4 skipped (rt_priv_* need the unbuilt ax66 engine).

commits.subject: platform: shared-mem RAM substrate (SimpleMemory + MmapBacking)
commits.notes: Adds mmap-backed main RAM so QEMU and vsim share one physical image across the handoff; maps one page above --mem-size for the V-scratch page.

commits.subject: hybrid: Debug Module access layer (abstract command + program buffer)
commits.notes: Low-level DMI transport: abstract-command GPR/CSR access + Program Buffer executor + dmi_poll; program_buffer.hpp is later slimmed to V/L2C-only by 80ab50d but the layer itself survives at tip.

commits.subject: hybrid: state loader + ABI guard
commits.notes: Loads the hybrid_state_v1 wire struct drained by the QEMU plugin and validates ABI size/offsets/flags so producer and consumer cannot drift.

commits.subject: hybrid: CSR/PC trigger + instruction matching
commits.notes: Detects the handoff boundary inside vsim: marker mode scans the ELF for the magic CSR-write HINT, PC mode arms an explicit exit PC.

commits.subject: hybrid: V regfile transport via scratch RAM
commits.notes: Moves v0..v31 through the scratch page at the top of the shared mmap (stage bytes, vle8.v load sweep, vse8.v drain sweep); the only PB register transport that survives to the Abstract-Command-only tip.

commits.subject: hybrid: ResumeDriver Tier A/B CSR restore + V reload
commits.notes: Writes drained state into the halted hart: GPRs/FPRs/M-mode CSRs via abstract commands (Tier A), vtype/vl via PB vsetvl (Tier B), V-data reload sweep; includes fcsr, VLEN ceiling rejection, dcsr.prv privilege, trap CSRs, mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl.

commits.subject: hybrid: StateDrain readback + V drain policy
commits.notes: Reads full architectural state back at the exit trigger; vse8.v dump sweep issued last so its clobbers cannot corrupt the record; introduces the RecordingBus duck-typed DMI test double.

commits.subject: hybrid: HandoffController phase dispatch + exit codes
commits.notes: Single-Trigger controller that watches retired PCs, drains on the exit trigger, and returns the handoff exit code; smoke tests exercise shared-mem offset math.

commits.subject: describe: --describe engine self-report (XLEN/VLEN/DLEN/ELEN)
commits.notes: Emits a JSON engine descriptor (id, kind, triggers, roles, state, invoke template) scanned from the embedded config.inc blob so the andesim driver can hot-plug the binary with no per-engine code.

commits.subject: integration: wire handoff into Simulator/main + hybrid CLI + HTIF VA fix
commits.notes: Wires apply_resume_from_qemu/enable_hybrid_handoff into the simulator, adds the hybrid CLI block (--shared-mem-*, --resume-from-qemu, --handoff-out, --hybrid-enter/exit-pc), and fixes HTIF file io to resolve through the resumed page tables.

commits.subject: build+docs: hybrid ctest registration + DM-coverage notes
commits.notes: Build/test wiring for the hybrid layer (ctest registration, check target) plus DM coverage notes and OpenOCD TCL; no standalone behavior, folds into the hybrid-core feature.

commits.subject: build: source the shared ABI from the andesim_abi submodule, not ../include
commits.notes: Pins the shared ABI as a nested submodule at external/andesim_abi so vsim builds standalone without reaching up into the superproject; structural change.

commits.subject: Andes V5 CSR transport: restore + re-drain (v3 ABI)
commits.notes: ResumeDriver restores the Andes CSR block under HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES via the X-macro tolerant-write loop + PMA (pmaaddr before pmacfg); StateDrain re-reads it at exit; bumps the ABI submodule to v3.

commits.subject: Gate Andes-CSR transport on per-engine capability
commits.notes: Introduces AndesCaps (CSR-address to feature-gate map built from the compiled-in _NDS_* config macros) so transporting a CSR the core lacks cannot hang the DM handshake; --describe now emits andes_csrs for driver verify-exclusion.

commits.subject: F2: transport the v4 M-ext CSR block (capability-gated)
commits.notes: Consumes HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST (51 writable M-mode CSRs, ABI v4) with the same X-macro pattern; adds 11 M-ext capability gates so premium enables exactly the 17 CSRs it implements.

commits.subject: F5: fix mcounterwen gate (UMODE, not PERF_MONITOR)
commits.notes: One-gate fix: mcounterwen exists only with user mode, so PERF_MONITOR gating made an M-only core drop the restored value and fail --verify; regates it UMODE.

commits.subject: feat: --print-qemu-config -- bake the engine's QEMU -readconfig cfg
commits.notes: Bakes a QEMU -readconfig cfg distilled from each engine's config.inc into the binary (via the new cpu_config_to_march_converter submodule) so the hybrid QEMU leg executes the same ISA the engine models; this is the branch-naming qemu-isa-match feature.

commits.subject: refactor(state_drain): extract halt() helper shared by drain paths
commits.notes: Structural prep for the counters-only drain: extracts the DM halt-and-wait prologue into a private halt(ctx) helper; survives at tip (shared by drain() and drain_counters_only()).

commits.subject: feat(hybrid): minimal drain (mcycle/minstret only) for unverified runs
commits.notes: Adds StateDrain::drain_counters_only() + --drain-minimal so --verify-off runs skip the ~190-command full readback (drain ~11.7s -> ~0.15s); survives at tip (80ab50d only drops the simulator's hybrid_drain_minimal_ member, the feature stays).

commits.subject: perf(hybrid): batch the V-data sweep into fewer Program-Buffer executions
commits.notes: Packs vle8/vse8+addi pairs per PB execution (33 -> 6 executions per direction, adds encode_addi); intermediate step largely rewritten by the next commit's LMUL=8 grouping, but the batching machinery (encode_addi, batched pb_v_data_sweep) survives at tip -- fold into v-transport.

commits.subject: perf(hybrid): LMUL=8 group the V-data sweep (4 loads in one PB execution)
commits.notes: Final shipped form of the V sweep: vsetvl e8/m8 + 4 grouped vle8.v/vse8.v moves all 32 V registers in one PB execution (scratch repacked at vlenb stride); survives at tip -- fold into v-transport.

commits.subject: fix(mem): make the final word of a memory region reachable (behavioral)
commits.notes: Adds MemoryRegion::contains_access (half-open bounds check) fixing an off-by-one that made a region's final word unreachable; motivated by the later-removed GPR ld-sweep but a general fix that survives at tip -- fold into the fb52ad0 memory substrate.

commits.subject: perf(hybrid): restore GPRs via a Program-Buffer ld-sweep (behavioral)
commits.notes: Opt-in set_gpr_block_load: stage x1..x31 in the scratch page and reload via a PB ld-sweep instead of 31 abstract commands; 80ab50d removes the entire GPR/FPR/CSR PB sweep family (set_gpr_block_load, gpr_scratch_fits, encode_ld all absent at tip), making transport Abstract-Command-only.
